newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney sees excellent H1 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney sees excellent H1 outlook.

text.p: Euro Disney's new chairman, Gilles Pelisson, said on Wednesday that the sales trend in the first quarter of 1996-97 signalled an "excellent outlook" for the Disneyland Paris theme park in the first half.
But Pelisson, who replaced Philippe Bourguignon last month after the former chairman went over to Club Mediterranee, reiterated that 1997 would be "a difficult year".

The company has said lease and financial expenses will rise by around 200 million francs ($35.2 million) this year, after having risen by 100 million francs last year, as it resumes payments that had been suspended as part of a 1994 financial restructuring.
Nonetheless, "the trend in the first quarter gives us an excellent outlook," Pelisson told the annual general meeting.
Sales in the October-December quarter rose to 1.13 billion francs from 1.01 billion.
Pelisson said Euro Disney, 39 percent-owned by The Walt Disney Co, would feel the benefits of lower costs and new development at the park from 1998.
He said Euro Disney would stick to its low price strategy this year to encourage attendance although "that may weigh on our margins". But he said some prices may be re-evaluated from 1998.
Pelisson said he was convinced that the group could further reduce operating costs this year.
